intro: Every counter on the home page is a claim, and a claim needs a definition: what exactly is counted, what is excluded, and when the number was last true. This page is that definition, and it holds every counter the study keeps — including the ones the home page does not show. When a number changes, the change lands here first, dated.

hero.note: The three cells at the top of the home page. Their figures are the same counter values the stat bar uses — they were hand-written HTML and drifted 25.5 hours and $42.00 behind it. A {counter-id} in 'say' is substituted with that counter's value.

cells.label: Paid for legitimacy
cells.say: The official price of a listing is $0. Three institutions petitioned; nothing bought.

cells.label: Time, the actual currency
cells.say: Logged to the half hour and published with the receipts. {dollars} spent in dollars.

cells.label: Price, per BYKO in USDC
cells.say: Reserve ratio of the BYKO/USDC pool on Base. No aggregator in the path.
cells.tol: read at this block · changes with every trade

counters.label: Hours logged
counters.counts: Working hours spent on the BYKO study since 2 Aug 2026: contract work, liquidity setup, the website, listing applications, wallet-flag appeals, support conversations, and writing. Tracked per session, rounded to the half hour. Self-reported estimate from the project diary; it will increase as the remaining episodes get logged.
counters.excludes: Thinking about BYKO in the shower. Only sessions with an artifact — a commit, a submitted form, a sent message — are counted.

counters.label: Dollars spent
counters.counts: Direct out-of-pocket cost of the study: $74.02 — the exact, verified, irreversible pool funding, burned along with the LP tokens — plus $49.27 of BYKO bought from the pool with project wallets, every purchase reconciled against the on-chain transaction history. The founder's own buys used to be excluded here as "votes, not costs"; the audit of 16 Aug 2026 counted them, because money that left the wallet is a cost whatever it was buying.
counters.excludes: The $5.57 returned by four small sells — this counts what went out, not the net — and the value of the time counted in hours above.

counters.label: Paid for legitimacy
counters.counts: Money paid for listings, promotions, fast-track reviews or any other route to visibility. Quoted so far and declined: $299 (DexScreener Enhanced Token Info), $195 (DEXTools), about $5,000 for CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap price data via the paid routes people quote, and BaseScan Priority Support, which sells a faster answer rather than an approval. The study's rule is that this number stays zero; if it ever changes, the diary explains why in full.

counters.label: Institutions petitioned
counters.counts: Organisations where BYKO submitted an application or opened a support case, and a response was received or awaited. That criterion, and nothing looser: BaseScan (token information form, 4 Aug, three waves of refusals), Crypto.com (support, four rounds on the missing icon, later the "fake" conversation), Coinbase (support, case #27207505) and Blockaid, filed after the wallet flags and answered twice in writing, on 19 and 20 Aug 2026 — the second reply giving the verbatim category, the reason code, and the criteria for reassessment. Counted once per organisation, however many rounds it took.
counters.excludes: Systems that issued a verdict on BYKO without ever being petitioned: MetaMask and Blockaid dropped the liquidity flag after rescanning the burn — in the diary's own words, "no email, no form, no appeal" — which is a separate thing from the Blockaid case later filed and counted above. Also excluded: free scanners the study ran itself (counted separately below), and services whose price list or requirements were only read — DexScreener, DEXTools, Trust Wallet.

counters.label: Listing approvals
counters.counts: Applications for public token information that ended in a stated approval: BaseScan answered “The token has been queued for update” for LUKO on 21 Aug 2026, after one template rejection and a rewrite of the description from manifesto language into plain facts. Counted when the service says yes, not when the page shows it — checked five days later, the page still does not.
counters.excludes: Paid fast-track offers (declined on principle — see Paid for legitimacy), approvals implied but never stated, and the update actually appearing on the page — that is a separate fact anyone can verify against the token page itself.

counters.label: Episodes published
counters.counts: Diary entries live on this site, counted from website/content/diary.md — the single markdown source every page is generated from. An episode counts when it is published, not when it is written.
counters.excludes: Drafts, and social posts that repeat an entry — an episode is counted once, however many times it is re-shared.

counters.label: Invoices settled in BYKO
counters.counts: Invoices for the author's own work that were priced in euro and actually paid in BYKO, counted once each, with the payment transaction hash recorded in the diary. The conversion uses the BYKO/USDC pool rate at the block named on the invoice, so anyone can reproduce it afterwards. Zero is the honest starting point of a new measurement, not a placeholder.
counters.excludes: Invoices settled in euro; quotes and conversations that never became an invoice; donations, which are a separate thing entirely and get a card instead.

counters.label: Trading-rule amendments
counters.counts: Amendments to the pre-registered self-trading rules (market/rules.json), counted from the numbered amendment record in the file's own note. Each one moves the canonical sha256 the worker checks before every trade, so each is a visible commit plus a deliberate hash update in the trading database.
counters.excludes: Code changes that do not touch rules.json, and parameter values the amendments left as they were. Silent retuning is excluded by construction: a rules edit whose hash was never updated halts both arms instead of trading.

counters.label: Listing rejections
counters.counts: Rejections counted per submission wave — a distinct submission date, not a distinct email: 04, 05 and 11 Aug 2026 for BYKO, and 07 Aug 2026 for LUKO's BaseScan Token Info application. One wave can answer with several template refusals the same day (one bundled four identical emails); it still counts once. A submission with no reply after the service's own stated review window also counts — silence is an answer.
counters.excludes: Forms never submitted, paid fast-track offers (declined on principle — see Paid for legitimacy), and resubmissions of the same form that are still inside the review window.

counters.label: Wallet flags
counters.counts: Wallet products that mark BYKO as risky or suspected spam by default, counted per product, verified by opening the token in the wallet and screenshotting the warning. Two stand. MetaMask's "Unstable price". And Base App's "scam", which was gone on 17 Aug 2026 and back by 19 Aug — screenshotted at 23:01 that evening, full-screen, on BYKO and on its control token LUKO, with the same two reasons on both. Base App's own sheet attributes the verdict to "security providers". Blockaid, the provider MetaMask reads, wrote on 20 Aug 2026 that for this token it returns Spam with the reason code unstable-price, that it is "not returning Malicious/Scam for this token", and that the Coinbase wording is "Coinbase's own classification (different vendor/policy)".
counters.excludes: Third-party allowlist databases the wallets read from — the flag is counted once, at the wallet where the user sees it.

counters.label: Flags removed
counters.counts: Warnings a wallet or scanner has actually stopped showing, counted per warning at the product where a user sees it, verified by reopening the token there. One: MetaMask's "Low locked liquidity", dropped by Blockaid about a day after the LP burn on 7 Aug 2026, with no email, form or appeal. This counter read two until 20 Aug 2026; the second was Base App's "scam" flag, gone on 17 Aug. It came back by 19 Aug and is on the screen now, so by this counter's own rule — a flag counts only when the warning is gone from the screen — it no longer qualifies and moves back to Wallet flags. A removal that was reversed is not a removal, and leaving it counted would have been the single most flattering error available.
counters.excludes: Warnings still displayed — MetaMask's "Unstable price" and Base App's "scam" — and removals promised in a reply but not visible in the product: a flag counts only when the warning is gone from the screen.
